answer: Admit each identity through a fixed TERRACE of fifty review slots per epoch, allocated by sealed burned bids. A NEBULA of clones under one operator must bid for many slots at once, and its aggregate demand lifts the clearing price it then pays on every slot it wins, so cost per added identity climbs with the farm's size. Spreading bids across later epochs only throttles it to the terrace's fixed width. Each bid is a SONNET, a rigid fixed-form record the ledger rechecks at settlement, burning any admission underpaid or shared. Doubling the farm more than doubles its burn.
